title: PagerDuty context proxy: attach timeline snippets and runbook seeds to urgent alerts
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: On high-severity incidents we often lose key context when alerts fire: traces are long-lived elsewhere, dashboards show noisy aggregates, and the on-call engineer needs a rapid, focused snapshot to act. Goal: build a lightweight PagerDuty context proxy that enriches triggered urgent incidents with three artifacts: 1) trace/timeline snippets (top 3 spans and related logs), 2) a seeded runbook link tailored to the service and symptom, and 3) a postmortem scaffold pre-filled with initial detection metadata. This ticket implements the server-side enrichment and a minimal opt-in toggle in PD integration settings; follow-ups will add richer UI in Console and Slack interactive buttons.
acceptance_criteria: When a PD urgent incident is created, the PD payload includes a context attachment with up to 3 trace snippets (span name, latency, error flag, trace URL),
Runbook seed URL is included that maps service + symptom to the correct playbook (fall back to generic playbook if unknown)
Postmortem scaffold is auto-created in our internal GH template repo with the incident key and an initial summary field, and the link is included in the PD attachment
Feature is behind an org-level toggle; default is off for existing customers and on for internal sandbox orgs
Rate limiting and PII redaction applied to attachments (no raw payloads, max 2 KB per snippet)
steps: Design PD context proxy API that subscribes to PD webhooks and fetches traces via tracing-hub service
Implement enrichment worker that extracts top spans and aggregated log snippets, applies redaction rules, and composes PD attachment payload
Add mapping table service for service->runbook and symptom classification (initially rules-based)
Create GH postmortem scaffold writer that uses the incidents repo template and returns a short link
Add integration tests and e2e test harness that simulates urgent PD incidents and validates attachments
Roll out behind feature toggle with telemetry metrics for success/failure of enrichment steps
comments: 2026-02-27 Priya Nair: Created ticket after postmortem for runtime outage; initial design doc linked. Key risk: exposing trace links with user PII. Proposal: redact event attributes and only include span name, duration, and a signed short trace URL with 1-hour TTL.

2026-03-02 Mateo Alvarez: Spike complete; worker prototype can pull traces and extract top spans in ~120ms for 95th percentile on staging. Observed costs: additional calls to tracing-hub ~0.7 requests/sec for a busy org. Added redaction module and size cap, initial PR opened.

2026-03-04 Design review (Samira Khan): Runbook mapping needs a fallback UX. Recommend including both 'Suggested runbook' and 'Alternative runbooks' when mapping confidence < 0.6. Also suggested adding an 'acknowledge from PD' button in a follow-up ticket.

2026-03-06 Security review (Avery Chen): Approved redaction rules but requested a formal threat model for trace link signing. Marked security_review_required=true and added pending task ENG-61911 for signing key rotation.

2026-03-09 QA (Jordan Li): Added e2e tests; found flaky case when tracing-hub returns partial traces. Implemented retry with exponential backoff and 'best-effort' flag so enrichment never blocks incident creation.

2026-03-12 Mateo Alvarez: Merged PR with enrichment worker and basic mapping table. Remaining: postmortem scaffold writer needs permissions to create GH issues in incidents repo; raised request to infra (INF-204). Plan to toggle-on for internal sandbox next week and monitor telemetry: enrichment_success, enrichment_latency_ms, redact_failures.
Notes: Keep message short in PD; avoid > 8KB payloads. Future follow-ups: Slack actionable pane, PD UI toggle per-policy, ML-based symptom classification (ENG-62999).
